title: Recyclable and Low Fat Products
summary: Return product ids where low_fats = 'Y' and recyclable = 'Y'.
approach: Simple WHERE with AND on both flags.

title: Find Customer Referee
summary: Customers whose referee is not 2, including NULL referees.
approach: Use referee <> 2 OR referee IS NULL — <> does not match NULL.
dialectNote: On LeetCode (MySQL) the same NULL logic applies.

title: Big Countries
summary: Countries with area >= 3M km² or population >= 25M.
approach: OR filter on two numeric thresholds.

title: Article Views I
summary: Authors who viewed their own articles more than once.
approach: Filter author_id = viewer_id, GROUP BY author_id, HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
solution:
SELECT author_id AS id
FROM Views
WHERE author_id = viewer_id
GROUP BY author_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

title: Invalid Tweets
summary: Tweet ids where content length exceeds 15 characters.
approach: CHAR_LENGTH or LEN on content column.
dialectNote: LeetCode uses CHAR_LENGTH; SQL Server uses LEN.

title: Rearrange Products Table
summary: Unpivot store columns into (product_id, store, price) rows.
approach: UNION ALL three SELECTs or UNPIVOT on store columns.
solution:
SELECT product_id, 'store1' AS store, store1 AS price FROM Products
UNION ALL
SELECT product_id, 'store2', store2 FROM Products
UNION ALL
SELECT product_id, 'store3', store3 FROM Products;

title: Replace Employee ID With The Unique Identifier
summary: Map legacy id to unique id via join.
approach: JOIN Employees to EmployeeUNI on id = employee_id.

title: Product Sales Analysis I
summary: Product name, year, and price for each sale.
approach: JOIN Sales to Product, project columns.

title: Customer Who Visited but Did Not Make Any Transactions
summary: Count visits with zero transactions per customer.
approach: LEFT JOIN transactions, filter NULL transaction_id, GROUP BY customer.
solution:
SELECT v.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS count_no_trans
FROM Visits v
LEFT JOIN Transactions t
  ON v.visit_id = t.visit_id AND v.customer_id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL
GROUP BY v.customer_id;

title: Rising Temperature
summary: Dates where temperature is higher than the previous day.
approach: Self-join on date + 1 day, compare temperatures.
dialectNote: LeetCode uses DATEDIFF; SQL Server uses DATEADD.
solution:
SELECT w1.id
FROM Weather w1
JOIN Weather w2
  ON DATEDIFF(day, w2.recordDate, w1.recordDate) = 1
WHERE w1.temperature > w2.temperature;

title: Find Followers Count
summary: Users with at least 1000 followers.
approach: GROUP BY user_id, HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000.
solution:
SELECT user_id
FROM Followers
GROUP BY user_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000;

title: Biggest Single Number
summary: Largest number that appears exactly once.
approach: GROUP BY num HAVING COUNT=1, then MAX.
solution:
SELECT MAX(num) AS num
FROM (
  SELECT num
  FROM MyNumbers
  GROUP BY num
  HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
) x;

title: Project Employees I
summary: Average experience years per project.
approach: JOIN and AVG grouped by project_id.
solution:
SELECT p.project_id, ROUND(AVG(e.experience_years), 2) AS average_years
FROM Project p
JOIN Employee e ON p.employee_id = e.employee_id
GROUP BY p.project_id;

title: Sales Analysis III
summary: Products sold only in first year (2018) and never in 2019.
approach: GROUP BY product, use MIN(year) and MAX(year) both = 2018.
solution:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name
FROM Sales s
JOIN Product p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING MIN(s.year) = 2018 AND MAX(s.year) = 2018;

title: Maximum Transaction Each Day
summary: Highest amount transaction per day (ties included).
approach: RANK or DENSE_RANK partitioned by day on amount.

title: Second Highest Salary
summary: Return the second highest distinct salary.
approach: MAX where salary < (SELECT MAX(salary)) or DENSE_RANK = 2.

title: Nth Highest Salary
summary: Function returning Nth highest salary.
approach: DENSE_RANK in subquery filtered to N.
solution:
-- LeetCode expects a function; core query:
SELECT salary
FROM (
  SELECT salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rk
  FROM Employee
) x
WHERE rk = @N;

title: Rank Scores
summary: Rank scores with ties (gaps after ties).
approach: RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC).

title: Consecutive Numbers
summary: Numbers appearing at least three times in a row.
approach: Self-join id+1 and id+2 with same num, or LAG window.
solution:
SELECT DISTINCT l1.num AS ConsecutiveNums
FROM Logs l1
JOIN Logs l2 ON l1.id = l2.id - 1 AND l1.num = l2.num
JOIN Logs l3 ON l2.id = l3.id - 1 AND l2.num = l3.num;

title: Employees Earning More Than Their Managers
summary: Employees paid more than their direct manager.
approach: Self-join employee to manager on managerId.
solution:
SELECT e1.name AS Employee
FROM Employee e1
JOIN Employee e2 ON e1.managerId = e2.id
WHERE e1.salary > e2.salary;

title: Duplicate Emails
summary: Emails that appear more than once.
approach: GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1.
solution:
SELECT email
FROM Person
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

title: Customers Who Never Order
summary: Customer names with no orders.
approach: LEFT JOIN orders WHERE order id IS NULL, or NOT EXISTS.
solution:
SELECT c.name AS Customers
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.customerId
WHERE o.id IS NULL;

title: Department Highest Salary
summary: Employee with max salary in each department.
approach: Join dept, filter salary = MAX per department.
solution:
SELECT d.name AS Department, e.name AS Employee, e.salary
FROM Employee e
JOIN Department d ON e.departmentId = d.id
WHERE e.salary = (
  SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee e2
  WHERE e2.departmentId = e.departmentId
);

title: Department Top Three Salaries
summary: Top 3 salaries per department (ties may yield more than 3).
approach: DENSE_RANK partitioned by department ORDER BY salary DESC <= 3.

title: Delete Duplicate Emails
summary: Keep one row per email (lowest id).
approach: DELETE where id not in min(id) per email group.
dialectNote: LeetCode allows DELETE with subquery; test on their editor.
solution:
DELETE p1
FROM Person p1
JOIN Person p2
  ON p1.email = p2.email AND p1.id > p2.id;

title: Game Play Analysis I
summary: First login date per player.
approach: GROUP BY player_id, MIN(event_date).

title: Game Play Analysis II
summary: Fraction of players who logged in on day 1 and day 2 after first login.
approach: CTE first login, count day+1 logins / total players.

title: Game Play Analysis III
summary: Players with login streak of at least 5 consecutive days.
approach: Date minus row_number grouping (islands pattern).
solution:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT player_id, event_date,
    DATEADD(day, -ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY player_id ORDER BY event_date
    ), event_date) AS grp
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT player_id, event_date FROM Activity) x
)
SELECT DISTINCT player_id
FROM d
GROUP BY player_id, grp
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

title: Game Play Analysis IV
summary: Percentage of players active each day in first 7 days after install.
approach: Self-join activity within 7-day window of first login.
solution:
WITH first AS (
  SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date) AS install
  FROM Activity GROUP BY player_id
)
SELECT a.event_date AS install_dt,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT b.player_id) / COUNT(DISTINCT a.player_id), 2) AS percentage
FROM first a
JOIN Activity b
  ON a.player_id = b.player_id
 AND b.event_date BETWEEN a.install AND DATEADD(day, 6, a.install)
GROUP BY a.event_date;

title: Managers with At Least 5 Direct Reports
summary: Manager names with 5+ direct reports.
approach: GROUP BY managerId HAVING COUNT >= 5, join for name.
solution:
SELECT e2.name
FROM Employee e1
JOIN Employee e2 ON e1.managerId = e2.id
GROUP BY e2.id, e2.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5;

title: Find Median Given Frequency of Numbers
summary: Median from frequency table.
approach: Running sum window to find middle position.
solution:
WITH expanded AS (
  SELECT num FROM Numbers
  -- expand by frequency in practice; LC schema uses freq column
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT num, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY num) AS rn,
    COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM expanded
)
SELECT AVG(1.0 * num) AS median
FROM ranked
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2);

title: Consecutive Available Seats
summary: Seat ids that are free and next to another free seat.
approach: Self-join on seat id difference 1 with both free.
solution:
SELECT DISTINCT c1.seat_id
FROM Cinema c1
JOIN Cinema c2
  ON ABS(c1.seat_id - c2.seat_id) = 1
 AND c1.free = 1 AND c2.free = 1
ORDER BY c1.seat_id;

title: Sales Person
summary: Salespeople with no orders for RED company.
approach: NOT EXISTS orders linked to RED company.
solution:
SELECT s.name
FROM SalesPerson s
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN Company c ON o.company_id = c.com_id
  WHERE o.sales_id = s.sales_id AND c.name = 'RED'
);

title: Triangle Judgement
summary: Rows where x+y>z, x+z>y, y+z>x.
approach: Three inequality checks in WHERE.

title: Shortest Distance in a Plane
summary: Minimum Euclidean distance between any two points.
approach: Self-join all pairs, compute distance, MIN.
solution:
SELECT ROUND(MIN(SQRT(POWER(p1.x - p2.x, 2) + POWER(p1.y - p2.y, 2))), 2) AS shortest
FROM Point2D p1
JOIN Point2D p2
  ON (p1.x <> p2.x OR p1.y <> p2.y);

title: Second Degree Follower
summary: Users followed by someone you follow.
approach: Join Follow to itself on followee/follower chain.

title: Exchange Seats
summary: Swap adjacent seat ids; last stays if odd count.
approach: CASE on id parity with neighbor id.
solution:
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM Seat) AND id % 2 = 1 THEN id
    WHEN id % 2 = 1 THEN id + 1
    ELSE id - 1
  END AS id,
  student
FROM Seat
ORDER BY id;

title: Customers Who Bought All Products
summary: Customers who purchased every product in catalog.
approach: GROUP BY customer HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product) = total products.
solution:
SELECT customer_id
FROM Customer
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_key) = (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Product);

title: Actors and Directors Who Cooperated At Least Three Times
summary: Pairs with 3+ joint movies.
approach: GROUP BY actor, director HAVING COUNT >= 3.
solution:
SELECT actor_id, director_id
FROM ActorDirector
GROUP BY actor_id, director_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;

title: Product Sales Analysis II
summary: Total sales quantity per product (no sales = 0).
approach: LEFT JOIN product to sales, SUM quantity.
solution:
SELECT p.product_name, ISNULL(SUM(s.quantity), 0) AS total
FROM Product p
LEFT JOIN Sales s ON p.product_id = s.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_name;

title: Project Employees II
summary: Most experienced employee per project (ties → lowest id).
approach: ROW_NUMBER by experience DESC, employee_id ASC per project.
solution:
SELECT project_id, employee_id
FROM (
  SELECT p.project_id, p.employee_id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY p.project_id
      ORDER BY e.experience_years DESC, p.employee_id
    ) AS rn
  FROM Project p
  JOIN Employee e ON p.employee_id = e.employee_id
) x
WHERE rn = 1;

title: Sales Analysis I
summary: Products with no sales in 2018.
approach: LEFT JOIN 2018 sales, filter NULL.
solution:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name
FROM Product p
LEFT JOIN Sales s
  ON p.product_id = s.product_id AND s.year = 2018
WHERE s.product_id IS NULL;

title: Sales Analysis II
summary: Products with sales in both 2018 and 2019.
approach: GROUP BY product HAVING both years in set.
solution:
SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name
FROM Sales s
JOIN Product p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN s.year = 2018 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN s.year = 2019 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0;

title: Highest Grade For Each Student
summary: One row per student with their max grade (ties → lowest course).
approach: ROW_NUMBER partition student order grade desc, course asc.

title: User Activity for the Past 30 Days I
summary: Daily active user count for last 30 days.
approach: Filter activity_date window, GROUP BY day.
solution:
SELECT activity_date AS day, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users
FROM Activity
WHERE activity_date > DATEADD(day, -30, '2019-07-27')
GROUP BY activity_date;

title: Market Analysis I
summary: Buyers in 2019 with no approve return in 2019.
approach: Join users/orders/items, filter year and return flag.
solution:
SELECT u.user_id AS buyer_id, u.join_date
FROM Users u
JOIN Orders o ON u.user_id = o.buyer_id
JOIN Items i ON o.order_id = i.order_id
WHERE YEAR(o.order_date) = 2019 AND i.item_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY u.user_id, u.join_date
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN i.is_return = 'approved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0;

title: Product Price at a Given Date
summary: Latest price per product on or before 2019-08-16.
approach: ROW_NUMBER partition product order change_date desc, filter date.

title: Immediate Food Delivery II
summary: Percentage of orders delivered immediately on first day.
approach: AVG of case when order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date.
solution:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * AVG(CASE WHEN order_date = customer_pref_delivery_date THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END), 2) AS immediate_percentage
FROM Delivery;

title: Monthly Transactions I
summary: Monthly approved trans count, total, and chargebacks per country/month.
approach: FORMAT month, conditional SUM for approved vs chargeback.
solution:
SELECT DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(trans_date), MONTH(trans_date), 1) AS month,
  country,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN state = 'approved' THEN 1 END) AS approved_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'approved' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS approved_total,
  SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'chargeback' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS chargeback_total
FROM Transactions
GROUP BY YEAR(trans_date), MONTH(trans_date), country;

title: Last Person to Fit in the Bus
summary: Last person who boards without exceeding 1000 kg cumulative weight.
approach: Running sum window, max turn where sum <= 1000.
solution:
SELECT person_name
FROM (
  SELECT person_name, turn,
    SUM(weight) OVER (ORDER BY turn ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS running
  FROM Queue
) x
WHERE running <= 1000
ORDER BY turn DESC
OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT 1 ROW ONLY;
